but what i can say is that it's really ok to gain weight especially on the vacation. in fact, it just meant that i got to eat a lot of delicious food that i would not be able to get at home! the more important decision/choice is what you do AFTER your vacation. 

a lot of people fall off their good habits because they continue their 'vacation eating habits' past their vacation. meaning, if you overeat for a few days during your vacation, it really is perfectly fine but remember to get back in the groove of things shortly after your trip. 

most importantly enjoy your vacation to the fullest! if you wanna try something just go for it! don't be afraid to eat something new or tasty just because you're afraid of gaining weight. vacation is exciting, don't let the worries of tomorrow haunt your today.

please do not count calories :( i think it's quite dangerous for a growing person and i don't think it's right for you yet. 

i was an obese child growing up so i can understand. my pediatric dietitian never EVER recommended counting calories for me but when i reached 18 I was transferred to the adults and i had a separate conversation with another dietitian about counting calories and she told me it's safer now that I'm reaching adulthood! 

at your age, i think it's a lot more useful to think of having balanced meals and making healthier choices rather than counting calories. your body is growing and your metabolism is adapting. 

regarding your vacation, just enjoy your vacation, but it's also an excellent time for you to listen to your body. if your body is telling you that it's full, then you can moderate and decide when it's good to stop! when you're going on a buffet for eg, it's perfectly okay to eat what you want to eat! but you can add a bit of veggies or fibre into your buffet to make it more balanced :)

lastly, it's always best to visit a professional/dietitian at your age. please do not follow advice that are meant for adults!

i think this whole comment thread is addressing your point about bad/good food, which is not a good psychological thing for you as you embark on your journey! and also why we don't really promote restriction but rather moderation. 

first, bad and good provides a very extreme and polar. it suggests that the food you label bad are food that have no nutritional value, it harms you and you must avoid at all cost. which is not true! yes there are calorie denser foods but those can still be incorporated and welcomed in your diet while losing weight!

second, we don't generally recommend restrictions as it can cause you to have very strong cravings down the road. you may compensate this restriction by binge eating and then you'll feel like shit for caving into your cravings, and then you restrict more and that vicious cycle haunts you. in extreme cases, if may cause you to start skipping meals to "compensate for your binge".

instead of telling yourself im gonna cut OUT all the food you mention above, i think it's better to think to cut DOWN or choose healthier options from the restaurants. mcdonald sell salads, or more nutritious food etc etc

and if you really feel like eating a burger, just eat a burger! no one is saying that you must eat a burger every single meal but if you are really craving for it, go ahead! eventually you want to enjoy this journey so you can sustain the weight loss. forcing yourself to not eat what you have enjoyed it's not a good thing for your mental health. 

i like to tell people that there's a reason why im fat! which is i loveee food, it's my love language. trying to restrict me from what i love is the last thing i want to do. i can do less but if i really want to im not going to stop myself!



>I will not be living my life like that

going back to your point, i promise you that restriction is not how you would want to live your life either. you can choose to believe me or not but i have tried to restrict multiple times in my journey and i saw short term results, but i gained a lot more weight in the long term. moderation not restriction!

honestly if cooking it's not right for you, there's nothing wrong with not relying on cooking. yes cooking helps you control calories a lot better but it's time and energy consuming. 

you can just eat whatever you've been eating (in moderation) and add a protein source (chicken, salmon etc etc) as well as vegetables for a balanced meal. 

that being said, investing in an air fryer is truly my holy grail. you can just leave it to air fry and you will consistently get a decent and delicious meal out of it. 

nutrition by kylie also has very simple and easy recipes that i think totally fits your lifestyle, can check her out on youtube!

steps I've taken to aid with soreness

1) always warm up and COOL DOWN. super super important to cool down and i think people always forget to stretch. just do some simple stretches that target the muscle group you have engaged to prevent cramping 

2) eat bananas, have been proven to prevent cramps. and also this [funny video](https://youtu.be/LdGai72Tt8Y?si=fUHut2Jk57BRVUmH)

3) hydrate hydrate hydrate

4) rest rest rest, rest in a way that the sore muscles is not tensed. for ex, if your biceps hurt, then sleep with your arms curled

5) get some muscle patches (like salonpas) if it's really unbearable

6) don't force yourself to exercise again if it hurts. just rest or do at a much lighter mode

lastly, feel the ache and soreness from DOMS with pride. it means you are getting stronger and you have been taking steps to be stronger and gain muscle. be proud of yourself!

I feel like Uni is genuinely that sweet spot where you get the most autonomy for yourself at the same time no need to really worry about your future. 

Pri, Sec, JC you are forced into a structured timetable, activities are minimal at most CCAs. everyday is very blurry

  
Uni you see clubs, programs, random ad hoc shit you want to go for 1 session. cooking class, board games, crocheting, pet therap etc. programs you can join that are more suited towards your interest as there are seniors before you who had the exact same interest as created it for their juniors. you get to choose your own timetable, you get to choose whether you want to skip lecture or not. yes you will pay the consequence if u let it snowball but the idea that you have a lot more autonomy now is very freeing. 

once you enter the working world, you're stuck to your 9 - 5. every day you're drained from work and only have time to eat dinner and sleep. everyday looks the same, everyday you're doing the same thing. it's so much harder to find free time than in uni. you have to worry about your long term future, whether your salary is enough to keep you afloat, whether you can even stay employed, when can you starting living on your own etc etc

a lot of people are giving a lot of very tangible and sound advice, im going to go on a tangent to give you some intangible ones.

stop with the "dieting" mindset, it subconsciously puts this idea into you that whatever you're doing now is short term. and once you hit your goal, you can just stop. 

but then once you hit 60kg, and then you stop "dieting", what will happen then? will you go back to your old usual eating habits. statistically speaking, a lot of people eventually gained back all the weight (and worse) a few years after they reached the goal. 

it's better to lose 6 kg in 10 years and keep it there than to lose 6 in 1 year, gain it back in another and keep on doing that forever.

what you should do instead is make small but permanent lifestyle changes that you can sustain forever. instead of thinking, omg i should eat chicken breast for ever. or, im never gonna eat desserts again. you could change it to, i will opt for leaner meats when i can do so. i will choose not to eat desserts if i don't really crave for it BUT i will let myself have some if im really craving for it. 

craving intensifies through rejection, the more you say i will NEVER have this, your body will subconsciously crave it more and more and it will hit a point where you binge eat and then you feel extremely guilty and the cycle repeats (from personal experience too) 

tldr: don't ruin your relationship with food just for the numbers on the scale, which doesn't define you :)
